title: Tower projection formula for compactly supported direct image over the standing field
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms; no further hypothesis on $k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$, and on a scheme $T$ let $A_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Use the varying-coefficient tower category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], its ordinary unbounded derived category with exact level evaluations $C_\bullet\mapsto C_n$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and its full subcategory $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ of towers whose levels lie in $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$ with cohomological and Tor intervals independent of $n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Derived tensor over the ring system $(A_{n,T})_n$, the termwise inverse images $u^{-1}$ along scheme maps (with the canonical identifications $u^{-1}A_{n,T}=A_{n,T'}$), derived direct images, termwise extension by zero along open immersions, and their adjunction units and counits are taken on the simultaneous section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism with a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, $j$ an open immersion and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $F_f=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ be the tower compact-support functor of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]; $j^{-1}p^{-1}=f^{-1}$. Let $C_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ and $B_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$; normalization is not assumed. Then $C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet$ and $j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet$ lie in $D^+$ of the tower categories, and in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(Y,\mathcal O_E))$ the two morphisms
$$F_fC_\bullet\otimes^LB_\bullet\xrightarrow{\ \pi_p\ }Rp_{*,\bullet}\bigl(j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet\bigr)\xleftarrow{\ Rp_{*,\bullet}(\pi_j)\ }F_f\bigl(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet\bigr)$$
are isomorphisms. Here $\pi_p$ is the proper projection map: the adjoint transpose, under $p^{-1}\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$, of the counit $p^{-1}Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\to j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$ tensored with $p^{-1}B_\bullet$, after the pullback/tensor comparison $p^{-1}(N\otimes^LB_\bullet)\simeq p^{-1}N\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet$. The map $\pi_j:j_{!,\bullet}(C_\bullet\otimes^Lj^{-1}p^{-1}B_\bullet)\to j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_\bullet$ is the open projection map: the transpose, under $j_{!,\bullet}\dashv j^{-1}$, of the unit $C_\bullet\to j^{-1}j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$ tensored with $j^{-1}p^{-1}B_\bullet$. Both are morphisms of derived towers, natural in $C_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$, and their $n$-th evaluations are the corresponding finite projection maps for the constant ring $A_n$. Hence $F_fC_\bullet\otimes^LB_\bullet\simeq F_f(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet)$ canonically and naturally.

proof.text: At level $n$ the coefficient ring $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$: writing $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ identifies it with $A_{E,en}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The two finite-discrete coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant], followed by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], identify module objects over the pulled-back condensed $A_n$ with ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring $A_{n,T}$. The equivalence preserves underlying sheaves. By [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] its termwise extension is an equivalence of unbounded derived categories preserving derived tensor, Tor intervals and the $\Dctf$ subcategories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and identifying the module-object $Rp_*D(j_!)$ with the ordinary $Rp_*j_!$. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] it identifies inverse image, direct image and open extension by zero with the ordinary ones, together with their adjunction units and counits. Since the equivalence is exact, the derived direct images, being derived functors of identified functors, also correspond, with their derived adjunctions. Hence the finite projection maps, formed from these tensors, pullbacks, direct images and units/counits, correspond as well. For finite $A_n$, finite constant local models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are exactly locally constant finite $A_n$-modules: a finitely presented module is finite, and a finite module has a presentation by finitely many generators whose relation module is finite, hence finitely generated. Thus the intrinsic finite constructibility and Tor tests in [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] are those of the finite-coefficient statements used below. The compactification stays in the standing separated finite-type setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting].

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite-level coefficient interpretation; finite-discrete Bhatt–Scholze coefficient comparison

proof.text: Choose uniform cohomological bounds $[a,b]$ for $C_n$ and a Tor interval $[u,v]$ for $B_n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. By [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model], represent $B_n$ by a flat complex $P_n$ supported in $[u,v]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]; its inverse images are K-flat with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback]. Good truncation represents $C_n$ by $T_n$ supported in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-truncations]; exact degreewise open extension gives the same bounds for $j_!T_n$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For either bounded representative $T$ and the corresponding pulled-back $P_n$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to T$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its acyclic cone stays acyclic after tensoring with the K-flat $P_n$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]; the total tensor of that cone is the cone of the tensored map, directly from the signed total differential. Thus $Q\otimes P_n\to T\otimes P_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The two-K-flat comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now shows that $T\otimes P_n$ computes the derived tensor. Its terms have degrees $r+s$ with $a\le r\le b$ and $u\le s\le v$, hence vanish outside $[a+u,b+v]$. Evaluation/tensor compatibility [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and levelwise kernels and cokernels [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] give this bound for both tower tensors. The same levelwise cohomology test puts $C_\bullet$, $B_\bullet$, and $j_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$ in $D^+$. These separate flat representatives only test bounds; they need not form a strict tower.

Use the simultaneous section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for the ring system $(A_{n,T})_n$. Its clause on the coefficient projection comparison constructs $\pi_p$ as the counit transpose specified in the statement, and its clause on open localization and transposes constructs $\pi_j$ from the open unit. These are actual morphisms of derived towers, natural in both inputs. Evaluation preserves tensor, composition, units/counits and taking these transposes by that same lemma; therefore $(\pi_p)_n$ and $(\pi_j)_n$ are exactly the corresponding finite proper and open projection maps, not arbitrary choices of levelwise isomorphisms. The comparison of clause 1 of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] identifies $(F_fD)_n$ with $Rp_*j_!D_n$ for each of the bounded-below inputs $D=C$ and $D=C\otimes^Lf^{-1}B$ obtained in step 2. These identifications also identify the evaluated map $Rp_{*,\bullet}(\pi_j)$ with $Rp_*((\pi_j)_n)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), actual tower projection maps; tower operations proof (1) and (2), coherent mate evaluation

proof.text: For every $n$, step 1 places $C_n$ and $B_n$ in the finite-coefficient $\Dctf$ categories. Since $j$ is an open immersion in the standing setting and $A_n$ is an admissible finite coefficient ring, [det-proper-image-localizing-open] gives $j_!C_n\in\Dctf(\overline X,A_n)$. Apply clause 3 of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite] to the proper morphism $p$, the input $K=j_!C_n$, and $M=B_n$. It says that the proper projection map $Rp_*j_!C_n\otimes^LB_n\to Rp_*(j_!C_n\otimes^Lp^{-1}B_n)$ is invertible. This is $(\pi_p)_n$ by step 3. Neither finite-coefficient theorem assumes that the standing field is algebraically closed or finite.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite proper projection; finite proper-base-change proof (3), Stacks Tag 0F0G

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] with $K=C_n$ and $L=p^{-1}B_n$. Its canonical finite open projection isomorphism is written in the direction $j_!C_n\otimes^LL\to j_!(C_n\otimes^Lj^{-1}L)$. Its inverse is the open-unit transpose $(\pi_j)_n$ of step 3: under $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ the latter map corresponds to $\eta_{C_n}\otimes1$, using the tensor/pullback identification, and composing with the displayed canonical comparison gives the adjunct of the identity by the unit/counit triangle identities. Thus $(\pi_j)_n$ is invertible. Applying the functor $Rp_*$ preserves its inverse, so every evaluation of $Rp_{*,\bullet}(\pi_j)$ is invertible as well.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite open projection and its direction; finite open projection proof via adjunction

proof.text: Clause 3 of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] detects isomorphisms in the unbounded ordinary derived category of towers. Steps 4 and 5 therefore make both $\pi_p$ and $Rp_{*,\bullet}(\pi_j)$ isomorphisms. Compose $\pi_p$ with the inverse of $Rp_{*,\bullet}(\pi_j)$ to obtain the asserted natural isomorphism $F_fC_\bullet\otimes^LB_\bullet\simeq F_f(C_\bullet\otimes^Lf^{-1}B_\bullet)$. The maps were natural before testing invertibility, so their composite with the inverse is natural too. No normalization or compatibility of independently chosen finite flat representatives is needed.
